item.title: Ensemble machine learning for crop classification
item.description:
Smallholder farmers cultivate more than 80% of Africa's cropland. Their fields are small, irregular and often intercropped, which makes crops very hard to map from space.

I developed a cloud-based, multi-temporal ensemble classifier in Google Earth Engine to map the most common crops on smallholder farms in southern Mali.

  • Combines spatial and spectral features from multi-temporal WorldView-2 imagery with field data.
  • Combines five machine learning classifiers using majority voting and weighted majority voting, and compares ensembles of different sizes.
  • Both ensemble strategies outperform every single classifier tested.

Read the paper: A Cloud-Based Multi-Temporal Ensemble Classifier to Map Smallholder Farming Systems, Remote Sensing 10(5), 729 (2018), with Raul Zurita-Milla, Emma Izquierdo-Verdiguier and Rolf A. de By.

item.title: Mapping public urban green spaces with open data
item.description:
Equitable access to green and public space is part of SDG 11.7, but up-to-date maps of public green spaces are rare, and existing approaches often depend on proprietary software.

This work builds a fully reproducible workflow using only Sentinel-2 imagery, OpenStreetMap data and open-source Python libraries, covering data acquisition, preprocessing, deep learning and evaluation.

Read the paper: City and Environment Interactions (2026).

item.title: ML4QGIS: machine learning inside QGIS
item.description:
ML4QGIS (Machine Learning for QGIS) brings machine learning for image classification and regression into QGIS, so geospatial analysts can train and apply models without writing code.

  • Available in the official QGIS plugin repository (version 0.4.0, August 2026), with more than 6,000 downloads.
  • Open source under GPL-3.0 on GitHub.
  • Introduced at FOSS4GNL 2025 and used in the FOSS4G 2026 workshop GeoAI Level Up, including YOLO object detection inside ML4QGIS.

Feedback, issues and pull requests are welcome.

item.title: OGITO: open tool for collaborative planning
item.description:
OGITO (Open Geospatial Interactive TOol) supports collaborative spatial planning on maptables: large horizontal touch screens that a group of stakeholders can use together.

  • Co-designed with planners and stakeholders using human-centred design and agile development.
  • Used for community mapping in Sumatra, Indonesia, and for noise action planning.
  • Code on GitHub; dataset on Zenodo.
  • Papers: CEUS 2020, Journal of Urban Technology 2023, and the PhD thesis.

item.title: Solar panels and electricity access from space
item.description:
• Built a YOLOv11 object-detection pipeline that detects solar panels in satellite imagery.
  • Built ML-ready training datasets from satellite imagery.
  • Developed Python workflows on VIIRS night-light imagery to identify solar facilities in rural areas.

item.title: Benchmarking AI agents for GIS
item.description:
AI agents are starting to operate GIS software on their own. How reliable are they on real geospatial tasks?

I lead the design of a benchmark that evaluates AI agents on geospatial tasks in QGIS. The benchmark questions are openly available on Zenodo.
